name: expenses
title: Expenses
description: Money the business spent, and sometimes money a client owes back. An expense is an accounting fact first and a billable item second, which is why it lives with the books rather than with the invoices: an unbillable expense still costs the company and still belongs in the ledger. It walks the same approval ladder as time (draft -> submitted -> approved -> billed) and for the same reason -- somebody other than the spender says yes before it becomes either a journal entry or a line on a client's bill. paid_by is the field most expense systems get wrong by omitting: a card the company holds and a card an employee holds produce DIFFERENT journals (credit the clearing account, or credit a liability owed back to the person), and guessing from the amount is not a strategy. markup_bps is in basis points to match invoice_lines' tax_rate_bps; it is stamped at approval alongside the billable amount, so re-running a bill can never apply this quarter's markup policy to last quarter's approved costs (docs/logic-decisions.md #1). Approved expenses are frozen: a mistaken one is corrected by a compensating entry or a credit, never by editing the record of what was spent (#5, #8).

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.help: What was bought. This is what a client reads on the invoice line, so write it for them.

fields.name: incurred_on
fields.label: Incurred
fields.help: The day the money was spent, which is the day the books belong to -- not the day somebody got round to entering it.

fields.name: amount_cents
fields.label: Amount
fields.help: What it cost, in integer minor units (docs/logic-decisions.md #10). The cost, not the price to the client.

fields.name: project_id
fields.label: Project
fields.help: What the spend was for. Required in practice to bill it: an expense with no project has no invoice to land on.

fields.name: account_id
fields.label: Expense Account
fields.help: Which account to debit. Falls back to the expenses.journal.expense_account setting, so a business that has not built out a chart of accounts still gets a balanced entry.

fields.name: paid_by
fields.label: Paid By
fields.help: company credits the card/cash clearing account. personal credits a liability owed back to the person who paid -- a reimbursement the business owes, which is a real debt and not a footnote.

fields.name: billable
fields.label: Billable
fields.help: Whether the client pays it back. Unbillable expenses still post to the books; they simply never reach an invoice.

fields.name: markup_bps
fields.label: Markup
fields.help: Basis points added when billing it on: 1500 is 15%. Deliberately has NO default, so that blank and zero can mean different things: blank takes the house policy (the billing.expense_markup_bps setting) at approval, while an explicit 0 says this one goes through at cost no matter what the house does. A default of 0 here would have made the two indistinguishable and quietly disabled the setting.

fields.name: billable_amount_cents
fields.label: Billable Amount
fields.help: Stamped at approval: amount plus markup, rounded half-up once. What actually reaches the invoice.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.help: Only the person who spent the money may submit it, and somebody else approves it. Approval is what composes the journal and what makes it billable. billed is terminal -- a disputed expense is a credit on the invoice, not a rewind.

fields.name: invoice_id
fields.label: Invoice
fields.help: Stamped when billed. An expense already carrying one is never billed again.

fields.name: receipt_ref
fields.label: Receipt
fields.help: Where the evidence lives -- a file id, a scan id, a vendor reference. Becomes a relation to scanned documents when document intake lands; kept as free text until then rather than declaring a relation to a collection that does not exist yet.
